rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God has appointed distinct ways for all creatures to glorify and pray to Him, and each has learned and follows its own way.
rows.anchor: He has appointed different ways for everyone to do so, and everything has fully learnt these ways and is following them accordingly.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: People need not know how birds glorify God: God knows all they do and reveals this so people can learn from it.
rows.anchor: God is aware of all they do, and it is God Who is informing them about this so that they seek a lesson from it.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God alone owns the universe and everyone returns to Him; therefore no one else deserves glorification or exaltation.
rows.anchor: None except God is the sovereign of this universe and none except to Him will everyone return.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The cloud passage proves God's absolute, wise control: He alone decides whether nature brings benefit or harm, preserves or afflicts, and no one can avert His trial.
rows.anchor: It is only He Who has absolute authority in it and none can interfere in His work which is solely based on His wisdom.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The passage's first part illustrates mercy and its hailstorm part affliction; violent winter clouds bring lightning and destructive hail, as in the punishment of some past nations.
rows.anchor: The first part exemplifies His mercy and the second (beginning wit the words: He unleashes from the sky) His affliction.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Only God controls the succession of day and night; no one can alter their arrival or departure, even by a fraction of a second.
rows.anchor: bringing forth the day after the night and the night after the day is solely in God’s control.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Insight reaches an inward reality through outward signs, and discovers principles concealed in particulars.
rows.anchor: the word ﻋmeans to reach one reality through another one.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: People of insight infer from these signs that a wise, powerful God created and governs the universe, and that He alone deserves worship and obedience.
rows.anchor: they have not the slightest doubt that this universe has been created by a wise and powerful God Who has sole authority in it.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Insight is the true substance of a human being; without it a person is like an animal, and an eye unable to see inner reality through outward form is blind.
rows.anchor: If someone is devoid of it, he is not a human being and is in fact an animal.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Differences among living forms do not imply multiple governing powers, as naïve idolaters claim; they instead demonstrate the Creator's power and wisdom.
rows.anchor: this does not mean that this universe is governed by different intentions, as is contented by the naïve idolaters.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: All living beings, whether two-legged or four-legged, come from the same water and therefore have the same Creator.
rows.anchor: He created all living beings from the same water. Who can say that the creator of two-legged animals is different and of four-legged ones different.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God creates any form He wills by His power; because He has power over all, everyone should entrust themselves to Him and worship Him alone.
rows.anchor: He creates whatever He wants to from His power in whatever form and shape He intends.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: This warning echoes verse 24 earlier: God guides through His revelations those who choose the straight path; the ungrateful remain in desire's darkness until their fate, while His wise, absolute will cannot be changed.
rows.anchor: This is a warning similar to the one sounded in verse 24 earlier.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: After the general call to submit to God, the passage turns to hypocrites whose mischief had grown, as the incident of ifk shows.
rows.anchor: After a general invitation had been given to the addressees to consign themselves to God, the case of the hypocrites is taken up.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The hypocrites' verbal profession is false without prompt obedience to God's and His Messenger's directives; refusal makes their claim wholly false.
rows.anchor: an essential requirement is to obey the directives of God and His messenger without any reluctance and hesitation.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Evading the Messenger's judgment in disputes proves hypocrisy; calling people to God means calling them to God's law, represented by the Messenger, whose verdict is God's verdict.
rows.anchor: Inviting people to God here obviously means inviting them to the law of God of which the messenger is a representative.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: When Jews held influence around Madinah, hypocrites used their courts because Jewish law had been altered and judges could be bribed; they chose the Prophet's court only when expecting a favorable ruling.
rows.anchor: if they had a hope to obtain a favourable decision from the Prophet (sws), they would very obediently take their dispute to his court

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: They approached the Prophet when expecting a favorable judgment and otherwise went to Jewish courts; Qur'an 4:63 calls seeking judgment from ṭāghūt a polytheistic practice.
rows.anchor: The Qur’ ān (4:63) has called this attitude of theirs as taḥākum il ā al- ṭāghūṭ (seeking verdict from Satan) and regarded it as a polytheistic practice

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The Qur'anic word “ailment” can mean jealousy or hypocrisy; context indicates hypocrisy here.
rows.anchor: The word ailment is used in the Qur’an to refer to both “jealousy” and “hypocrisy.” Concomitant indications show that here it refers to the latter.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Irtiyāb means being afflicted with doubt; the doubt may concern Muhammad's messengership or Islam's future, making hypocrites hedge between the two sides.
rows.anchor: The word إرﺗﻴﺎبmeans to be inflicted with doubt. This doubt can relate both to the messengerhood of Muḥammad (sws)

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The word ḥayf means oppression and injustice.
rows.anchor: The word ﺣﻴﻒmeans “oppression and injustice.”

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Their hesitation reflects one or all of three failings: hypocrisy, doubt about the Prophet or Islam's future, and fear of an unjust judgment; every possibility contradicts faith.
rows.anchor: either their hearts are inflicted with the ailment of hypocrisy or they are in doubt about the future of Islam and the Prophet (sws)

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: They fear injustice from God and His Messenger, yet their own evasion wrongs themselves; they imagine they protect their interests while sheltering under a wall about to collapse.
rows.anchor: they fear injustice from God and His Prophet whereas by adopting this attitude they themselves are being unjust to themselves.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: True believers entrust themselves to God despite their own desires and thereby protect their interests in both worlds; those trying to straddle belief and disbelief are doomed.
rows.anchor: People who consign themselves to God disregarding their desires and wants, it is they who have in fact safeguarded their interests

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The form reduction in yat-taqhi changes its shape, and such reductions are common.
rows.anchor: has changed its shape, but such form reductions are common.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Islahi reads the adjacent terms for fearing God and observing His limits as inward fear in the heart and outward adherence to God's bounds.
rows.anchor: In my opinion, the former is a depiction of the state of the heart and the latter refers to abiding by the limits of God.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Success requires obeying God and His Messenger in easy and adverse circumstances, with a God-fearing heart and daily observance of His bounds; profession or obedience alone is insufficient.
rows.anchor: a mere claim to faith is not sufficient for success and salvation; obedience to God and His Messenger is also essential for this.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Selfish people who stay with God and His Messenger only to protect personal interests have no real commitment to them.
rows.anchor: the mean and selfish who want to remain with God and His Messenger merely to protect their personal interests

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Hypocrites who had boasted of readiness for jihad evaded it; the Prophet is told that oaths cannot replace ordinary obedience, and God knows their words and deeds.
rows.anchor: oaths are no substitute for deeds. The real thing that is needed from them is obedience to God and His Messenger according to the norms.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Hypocrites use abundant oaths because they lack noble traits to prove their character; earlier and later suras also mention this behavior.
rows.anchor: they do not have noble traits to prove their character; in order to do so, they use their oaths
